name: iMessage / SMS

tiers.how: Texts go out from the owner's iPhone through an Apple Shortcut that polls an outbox file managed by `assistant/scripts/phone_bridge.py`. The owner must install and enable the Shortcut on their iPhone; no API key or app password is needed. Once a text is placed in the outbox it is treated as sent, because the phone never sends an acknowledgment back to Sage.
reads: nothing; iMessage cannot be read programmatically on iOS without a Mac bridge
writes: outbound SMS or iMessage to any number placed in the outbox
always_tap: any outbound text to a lead or client that is not on the standing-text allowlist

gotchas: The phone never acknowledges delivery; once a text enters the outbox it is treated as sent.
Verify receipt only through a client reply, never through a system confirmation.
The four-hour chase window applies: do not re-send a text on 'unconfirmed' status alone.
A Mac-only alternative via AppleScript to Messages.app exists but requires the Mac to be awake and logged in.
Standing client texts (intro, collection-sent, questionnaire reminder, check-in, day-before, Finishing Touches) go out without an approval card; all others require one.
notes: iMessage is used for quick personal client touchpoints; it is fragile device automation and should not be the sole channel for any critical communication.
